about: Stock honeypot fingerprints a capture can show (docs/architecture/investigation-framework.rst, Honeypots). One match is never enough: a real server can send the same banner. strength: strong = only a honeypot sends it; medium = rare on a real server; weak = a real product's own default too. kind: ssh-banner, ssh-hassh, ftp-banner, http-server, smb-os, smb-server-name, mysql-version (from service_banners) and tls-cert (subject or issuer). match: equals or contains, case-sensitive.

signatures.why: Cowrie's default SSH version string (cowrie/cowrie, 2026); a real Debian 12 server sends it too
Cowrie's default SSH version string before 2.x; a real Debian 7 server sent it too
Kippo's default SSH version string; a real Debian 5 server sent it too
the HASSH of Cowrie's SSH key exchange (Twisted Conch, cowrie/cowrie 2026), which no OpenSSH release offers
Dionaea's self-signed default certificate (O=dionaea.carnivore.it, CN=Nepenthes Development Team)
Dionaea's default SMB native OS and LAN manager (dionaea/smb/extras.py); a real Windows XP sends the same
Dionaea's default FTP greeting (dionaea/ftp.py); a real Synology DiskStation sends it too
Dionaea's default MySQL version (dionaea/mysql/var.py); a real MySQL 5.7.16 may send it too
Glastopf's HTTP Server header (Vetterl and Clayton, 2018); a Python 2.5 web server from 2006 is rare
Amun's HTTP Server header (Vetterl and Clayton, 2018); a real Apache 1.3.29 sends it too
